from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Light acts as an electromagnetic wave.",
            "Waves possess both amplitude and phase.",
            "Superposition creates interference patterns.",
            "Constructive interference adds peak to peak.",
            "Destructive interference cancels peaks out."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light", lecture_lines)
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        wave = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=r, stroke_width=2, color=BLUE) for r in [0.5, 1.0, 1.5]])
        self.place_at_grid(wave, "C3", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(wave), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        label_a = Text("Amplitude", font_size=16, color=YELLOW).next_to(wave, UP)
        self.play(FadeIn(label_a), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        interference = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=r, stroke_width=2, color=RED).shift(RIGHT*0.5) for r in [0.5, 1.0, 1.5]],
                             *[Circle(radius=r, stroke_width=2, color=RED).shift(LEFT*0.5) for r in [0.5, 1.0, 1.5]])
        self.place_at_grid(interference, "D4", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(interference), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        const = VGroup(Dot(color=GREEN), Dot(color=GREEN)).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(const, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(const), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GREEN))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        dest = VGroup(Line(LEFT*0.2, RIGHT*0.2, color=PURPLE), Line(UP*0.2, DOWN*0.2, color=PURPLE))
        self.place_at_grid(dest, "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(dest), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Photographs capture only light intensity.",
            "Holography records the interference pattern.",
            "Reference beams provide constant phase.",
            "Object beams reflect off the subject.",

        ]

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Holography Mechanism: Reconstruction", [
            "Reconstruction uses the reference beam.",
            "The hologram acts like a key.",
            "Original wavefronts emerge from diffraction.",
            "This reconstructs the 3D volume.",
            "Viewing angles shift perspective accurately."
        ])

        # Define objects
        hologram = Rectangle(width=2, height=3, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        ref_beam = Line(LEFT*2, RIGHT*2, color=YELLOW)
        reconstructed_obj = Sphere(radius=0.5, color=RED).set_fill(RED, opacity=0.6)

        # Position objects
        self.place_at_grid(hologram, 'C4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(ref_beam, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(reconstructed_obj, 'B5', 'E6', scale_factor=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(ref_beam))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(FadeIn(hologram))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        # Animate diffraction effect
        diffraction_waves = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1+i*0.1, color=GREEN, stroke_opacity=0.5-i*0.1) for i in range(5)])
        diffraction_waves.move_to(hologram.get_center())
        self.play(Create(diffraction_waves))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(RED)
        self.play(FadeIn(reconstructed_obj))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(ORANGE)
        self.play(reconstructed_obj.animate.shift(LEFT*0.5 + UP*0.2), run_time=2)

outline.topic: The Magic of Light: Principles of Holography and Diffraction

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light
sections.content: Briefly review wave superposition and phase coherence. Explain that light is an electromagnetic wave characterized by amplitude and phase (the 'position' of the wave peak).
sections.example: Visualizing a ripple in a pond: how two ripples meeting create a complex pattern of peaks and troughs (constructive vs. destructive interference).

sections.title: Understanding Diffraction
sections.content: Define diffraction as the bending of waves around obstacles. Introduce the mathematical concept using the Fourier Transform: the diffraction pattern is the spatial frequency representation of the object.
sections.example: A laser pointer shining through a thin mesh (like a screen door) to produce a grid of dots—the 'diffraction pattern' encodes the shape of the mesh.

sections.title: The Holography Mechanism: Recording
sections.content: Explain that while photos only capture intensity (amplitude), holography captures interference patterns. Introduce the 'Reference Beam' vs. 'Object Beam' concept to record phase information.
sections.example: An animation showing two light waves meeting on a photographic plate, creating a 'frozen' interference pattern that looks like static noise but contains 3D data.

sections.title: The Holography Mechanism: Reconstruction
sections.content: Explain that shining the original reference beam back through the developed hologram acts like a 'key,' diffracting the light to recreate the original wavefronts.
sections.example: Imagine a 3D hologram of a rotating Iron Man helmet: as you walk around the hologram, you see different sides of the helmet because the phase-encoded light reconstructs the original spatial volume.

sections.title: Synthesis and Applications
sections.content: Connect the math (Fourier optics) to real-world technology. Summarize how diffraction enables the storage of 3D space on a 2D surface.
sections.example: Modern applications: Holographic data storage for long-term archival or high-security authentication on credit cards.
